_description: Real wall-clock recovery from a peer that vanishes mid-job.
The agent holding a running lease is SIGKILLed with no chance to release
it, and its trainer container is killed too — on a peer that really
disappears, the container goes with the machine. Nobody is left alive to
report anything, so the orchestrator has to detect the loss itself via
phi-accrual heartbeat silence (ADR-004), expire the lease, and reassign.
Deliberately NOT a docker kill of the trainer alone: that is a *reported*
failure, which services/leases.py makes terminal by design so a broken job
spec cannot loop across the fleet. Killing the container measured a job
going straight to FAILED at epoch 1 and recovering nothing. The retryable
case is a dropped node, and that is what this measures.
epochs is > 1 so the job outlives the warmup; a job that finished before
the kill would measure nothing, and the scenario fails loudly rather than
